title: Data Storytelling & Communicating Uncertainty
interviewAnswer: Data storytelling means structuring evidence around the decision: context, key finding, uncertainty, alternatives and recommended action. It is not decorating charts or hiding caveats.
why: Data Storytelling & Communicating Uncertainty is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
deepDive: Data storytelling means structuring evidence around the decision: context, key finding, uncertainty, alternatives and recommended action. It is not decorating charts or hiding caveats. Quantify uncertainty and practical magnitude. Separate observed facts from interpretation. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Present an experiment as “+1.2pp conversion, 95% CI 0.4–2.0pp, no latency regression,” then explain expected annual impact and risks.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Data Storytelling & Communicating Uncertainty?
How would you validate or tune Data Storytelling & Communicating Uncertainty?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.

visual.title: When geography is the story
visual.caption: Maps are useful when spatial pattern is part of the question; if the goal is precise ranking or magnitude comparison, a bar chart is often clearer.
